# 09 — Grow a large file across writes, and leave the branch clean

Status: ready-for-agent

**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately.

**What to build:** an **implementer** whose deliverable is a large generated file stops dying on it, and leaves nothing
behind that the next agent has to guess about. Two agents in an observed run died at the same point emitting a 700–900
line file in one write, discarding 760,091 billable tokens between them, and the ticket landed once a third was told to
grow the file instead. A fourth left an uncommitted 12.7 KB draft on disk that its retry rewrote — finding two real
shell bugs in it — but only because the orchestrator thought to flag it. Settled as D17 and D18 in `../spec.md`.

- [ ] `implementer` says to build a large generated file across several writes rather than emitting it in one call.
- [ ] It says to commit as soon as a coherent piece exists, and why: an interruption then costs minutes rather than the
      ticket.
- [ ] Step 4 admits more than one commit. Its closing condition says "that commit", singular, and the step sits after a
      step 3 that implements everything — so the rhythm above has nowhere to live until the step says it runs
      repeatedly, interleaved with step 3, rather than once at the end.
- [ ] It says the branch ends with nothing uncommitted of this agent's own work.
- [ ] Pre-existing uncommitted work is untrusted input: where it falls inside this ticket, it is re-derived rather than
      adopted as it stands.
- [ ] Uncommitted work outside this ticket's scope is reported and left untouched — not adopted, not committed, not
      discarded — because re-deriving another ticket's work is not this agent's job and destroying it is worse. The
      consequence is stated rather than hidden: such work stays on the branch, where a round may still read it.
- [ ] The reason a clean branch matters beyond tidiness is stated, in the form that is measured rather than inferred:
      the review may read the local working tree instead of the change request — observed on a non-GitHub forge — so
      uncommitted work is work a round may silently review. `plugin/mcp/server/agent-backend.ts` carries the mechanism
      in its header comment; the sentence in the contract need not assert a cause beyond that.
- [ ] The **Resume** paragraph no longer reads as licence to ignore a dirty tree. "The commits on the epic branch are
      what say how far it got" is true of what is *done* and silent on what is merely *present*, which is the sentence
      an agent followed when it left the 12.7 KB draft behind.
- [ ] The commit format is unchanged — the `Ticket:` line on every commit, and the `Assumptions:` and `Gates:` sections
      as they are.
- [ ] The delivery skill stops reading a present `Ticket:` line as a ticket *finished*, because more than one commit
      per ticket is what this ticket introduces: an implementer that dies after its first coherent piece leaves
      `Ticket: 7` on the branch, and **Resume** ("the commits carrying a `Ticket:` line name the tickets implemented")
      and **Progress**'s numerator ("how many tickets the `Ticket:` lines name, so a resumed run opens at the count it
      left off") would then count ticket 7 delivered, dispatch ticket 8, and flip a change request ready with a ticket
      half done. The line names a ticket **begun**; a resumed run re-dispatches the last ticket named as well as the
      ones with no commit at all, which needs no judgement — `implementer`'s own step 2 reports the commit that covered
      it where the branch already covered it in full (PR #4 review).
- [ ] Register is matched, and the file's column width is held: `implementer.md` wraps at 120 characters throughout
      with no line over, and every line this ticket writes or rewraps stays that way. Count characters, not bytes —
      the file's em-dashes are three bytes each, so a byte-based check reports overruns that are not there.

## Comments

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

**Triage, 2026-08-23 — stays `ready-for-agent`; the checklist was structurally broken, and four questions are settled.**

**The blocking defect was mechanical, not editorial.** The file carried seven `- [ ]` markers of which only two began a
line: a reflow to 120 columns had run the list together as though it were prose, so item 1 ended mid-sentence with
`...in one call. - [ ] It` and four markers survived only as literal inline text. Rendered as markdown that is **two**
bullets, not seven. Triaged sibling 08 is eleven-for-eleven by comparison. An agent taking this ticket would have read
two acceptance criteria and delivered against them, and the four instructions buried inside bullet one — commit early,
nothing uncommitted, untrusted input, the clean-branch reason — are precisely the ones D18 turns on. The list is now one
item per line with continuation indent.

**Nothing in `plugin/` implements any of this, and no other ticket touches the file.** Searched by domain concept rather
than by the request's wording: `uncommitted|working tree|stash|dirty`, `git status`, and `one write|single write|large
file|incremental` across the whole plugin return nothing. No `.out-of-scope/` knowledge base exists, so there is no
prior rejection to weigh. Every other ticket in this set that says "implementer" means the role in prose — ticket 09 is
the only one writing to `plugin/agents/implementer.md`. Ticket 11 borrows the implementer's **assumption** entry shape
for `comments-addresser`, which is a read and not a write, and this ticket leaves the commit format alone; ticket 07
deliberately places its change in the delivery skill and keeps it out of **Resume**. Nothing to sequence against.

**What verified, and what did not.** The 700–900 line single write and the two-agents-at-the-same-point claim check out
against `../spec.md`. D18's mechanism verified *sharper* than the ticket stated it: `agent-backend.ts` records in its
header that *"A bare ref reviews the local working diff and finds nothing, because the change request's commits are not
in that tree"*, and user story 14 already carries the rationale almost verbatim. But the ticket's two most vivid figures
— 760,091 tokens, and the 12.7 KB draft whose rewrite found two real shell bugs — appeared **nowhere** except this
ticket. Not in the spec, not elsewhere in the tree, and not in git history, the directory being untracked. Sibling 08's
triage certified that every figure in it checked out against the spec; that bar was not met here, and the shell-bugs
anecdote is the only concrete evidence the re-derive criterion has. On your call they are now carried down into the
spec's problem statement, beside the 1,333,341 they break down, so the ticket cites rather than asserts them. Their
provenance is recorded honestly: the ticket was their only source, and nobody has re-verified them against the run.

**The stated cause was not the verified cause, and criterion 5 made an implementer write it into a shipped contract.**
The ticket said the review reads the local tree "where the review cannot fetch the change request". The server always
builds `--comment <url>` — there is no bare-ref path in shipped code — and what was measured on GitLab is that
`--comment` is *ignored*, which is about posting. Neither is "cannot fetch". Left alone, an implementer would have
written a causal claim about a third-party command that nothing in this repository establishes. The criterion now states
the observed effect and points at the header comment for the mechanism.

**Two structural collisions the criteria would otherwise have walked into.** Step 4 reads as a single terminal beat
after step 3 has implemented everything, and closes "the branch on the remote carries **that commit**" — singular, while
the commit-format section already says "every commit you make". Commit-as-you-go has nowhere to live in that shape, so
on your call step 4 goes plural and says it runs repeatedly, interleaved with step 3, keeping the numbered spine intact
rather than folding committing into step 3. And **Resume** says "The commits on the epic branch are what say how far it
got" — true of what is done, silent on what is merely present, and therefore the exact sentence an agent could follow
while leaving a draft on disk. It gets its own criterion rather than being left to fall out of the others.

**Foreign uncommitted work is reported and left, and the cost of that is stated.** "The branch ends clean" and
"pre-existing uncommitted work is re-derived" together do not say what happens to uncommitted work belonging to another
ticket, and an implementer would have had to guess between adopting it, committing it and deleting it. On your call it
is reported and left untouched: re-deriving another ticket's work is not this agent's job, and having the implementer
destroy work it did not write is a worse failure than the one D18 is fixing. The honest consequence is that D18's
guarantee is now partial — foreign uncommitted work stays on the branch, and a round on a forge that reads the local
tree may still review it. The criterion says so rather than implying the branch is unconditionally clean.

**Recorded, not actioned.** `spec-writer` and `tickets-writer` write large files under the same death risk — this repo's
own spec is 33 KB — and D17 scopes the instruction to the implementer's contract, so they are noted here rather than
changed. No ADR: a contract sentence is trivially reversible, and D17 and D18 already hold the decision. No glossary
work either — "the branch ends clean" is plain description, not a domain term, and every term the criteria lean on
(**assumption**, **fork**, **gate**, **round**, **change request**) is already in `CONTEXT.md`.
